articles.author: Stephan Bisaha
articles.description: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage reached 6.66% on average Thursday.
articles.title: Mortgage rates hit their highest level in a year, driven by war and inflation concerns

articles.author: Ari Daniel
articles.description: The accusations against Dr. Anthony Fauci, once the nation's leading infectious disease expert, have some experts worrying that these events may further erode public health staffing in the U.S.
articles.title: After Fauci Senate hearing, experts worry about 'chilling effect' on public health

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: Congress allocated $150 million for 250th birthday events. The Trump-backed group that planned the state fair and July 4th fireworks is asking for an additional $10 million in reimbursements.
articles.title: The Trump administration wants $10 million more to cover its July Fourth celebrations

articles.author: NPR Staff
articles.description: Solo living, solo travel, and solo dining are all being embraced as more adults are choosing to remain single. Many Americans aren't interested in dating, and being single is a symbol of autonomy.
articles.title: Are you choosing to stay single? We want to hear from you

articles.author: Rafael Nam
articles.description: European soccer associations said they would boycott the World Cup unless FIFA reverses a controversial deal to sell minority stakes to the marquee soccer tournament.
articles.title: European soccer leaders to boycott  the World Cup in an unprecedented step

articles.author: Danielle Kurtzleben
articles.description: The news comes as two key Republicans are withholding their support over concerns about the Justice Department's deal with President Trump.
articles.title: Trump says he 'may' pull Blanche AG nomination temporarily

articles.author: Scott Horsley
articles.description: The U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 1.5% in the spring, according to the Commerce Department. That's a modest slowdown from the previous quarter — but consumer spending picked up steam.
articles.title: The economy slowed a bit -- but Americans continued to spend

articles.author: Carrie Johnson
articles.description: Congress created the Alien Terrorist Removal Court in 1996 to make it easier for the Justice Department to use classified evidence to deport people from U.S. soil.
articles.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court holds its first-ever hearing after 30 years

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: A Russian missile and drone barrage across Ukraine killed at least 10 civilians, including children, and NATO scrambled jets after one of the missiles crossed the border into Poland.
articles.title: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10 and a missile falls in Poland

articles.author: Andrew Jones
articles.description: Robeson County, N.C., where most of the Lumbee Tribe's citizens live, ranks as one of the worst counties in the U.S. for health. The tribe can access the Indian Health Service now, but it's not likely to be sufficient to improve the health of the community.
articles.title: The Lumbee Tribe of N.C. wants better healthcare, but plans to fund it are in limbo

articles.author: Adam Fulton (now); Lucy Campbell, Maya Yang, Yassin El-Moudden, Tom Ambrose and Taz Ali (earlier)
articles.description:
US president claims his Board of Peace has reached ‘historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza’

US launches fresh strikes on Iran after days-long pause, amid fears the war is widening

A liquefied natural gas tanker controlled by QatarEnergy exited the strait of Hormuz overnight – the first such vessel ⁠visible on ship-tracking data to ⁠leave the waterway ​since 11 July, data from analytics firms showed on Thursday.
The Al Areesh tanker, which loaded a cargo at Qatar’s Ras Laffan terminal around 4-6 July, sailed ⁠out of the strait overnight on 29 July, according to Kpler and LSEG data.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump claims breakthrough reached in Gaza disarmament; Hamas confirms deal

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Former premier’s brother to appear before inquiry. Follow live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

eSafety commissioner says court action against Telegram ‘very significant’
Julie Inman Grant, the eSafety commissioner, spoke to the ABC this morning after yesterday’s court action against Telegram over its alleged failure to detect and remove pro-terror material from its platform.
The scars are still very raw around Bondi. … These are platforms – and they may be doing more content moderation and we would encourage that – but not to the degree that Australian law requires them to.
This is just upping the ante and it’s much more serious. And if they don’t comply when the court finds, or if the court finds against them, then they’ll be in contempt.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: Conservative Liberals group member tells Icac he can’t recall Taylor making donation, saying ‘I don’t think Angus worked out’

articles.author: Ima Caldwell
articles.description:
Queensland police fine driver of another car that allegedly caused Yaris to swerve before it hit kerb and catapulted into air – and bus
A Queensland driver has been fined after being involved in a stunning crash that saw a car become airborne and then stuck in the side of a bus.
The drama unfolded at Rocklea in Brisbane’s south on Wednesday evening. A blue Toyota Yaris hit a traffic island and was catapulted into the air before smashing into the side of the council bus. The back of the car was left protruding from the bus.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A car in the bus!’: Toyota becomes airborne and then wedges in side of Brisbane bus

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
One Nation leader’s ‘how can you tell me there are good Muslims?’ remarks were the subject of complaints, but police say the matter has now been finalised

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian federal police has determined One Nation leader Pauline Hanson’s comments about Muslim Australians “do not meet the threshold” of breaching hate laws.
The AFP said it received several complaints about Hanson’s remarks to Sky News on 16 February.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pauline Hanson’s comments on ‘good Muslims’ don’t breach hate speech laws, Australian federal police finds

articles.author: Staff and agencies
articles.description:
US president’s Board of Peace hails ‘critical step’, but responses of Israeli and Hamas officials suggest disagreements remain

Middle East crisis – live updates

What is Trump’s Board of Peace and who is involved?

Donald Trump has said a deal has been reached for Hamas to disarm and for Israel to withdraw its forces from Gaza, however briefings from both sides exposed disputes over its implementation that could prove difficult to overcome.
“This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people,” Trump said in a social media post.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Anna Betts, Shannon Ho, Lucy Campbell, Rachel Leingang and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
Republicans senators Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted in favor of the motion to prevent Trump from continuing hostilities against Iran. This blog is now closed.

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

The US economy expanded at a sluggish 1.5% pace from April through June as rising imports weighed on growth. But consumer spending rose. And the Federal Reserve’s favored measure of inflation grew more slowly last month despite remaining above the central bank’s 2% target.
The commerce department reported today that growth in US gross domestic product (GDP) – the nation’s output of goods and services – decelerated from 2.1% in the first three months of 2026 and came in below economists’ expectations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senate’s latest effort to halt Trump’s Iran hostilities fails in 49-50 vote as some Republicans side with Democrats – as it happened

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Company says it discovered unauthorized access during ‘proactive review’ after rival OpenAI revealed rogue agent
Anthropic ⁠said on Thursday its AI Claude model hacked ⁠systems of ⁠three ​organizations during testing, days after rival OpenAI ⁠revealed a rogue agent had gone on a days-long ⁠hacking spree at AI ​firm Hugging ‌Face.
Claude gained ‌unauthorized access to the ‌systems during cybersecurity evaluations after a misconfiguration allowed the models to reach the internet from testing environments that ‌were supposed to be isolated, Anthropic said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anthropic’s AI Claude escaped testing environment and hacked organizations

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Officers in murder trial testify of arriving at Massachusetts home after anguished 911 call from Patrick Clancy
The two police officers focused first on Lindsay Clancy drifting in and out of consciousness in the snow after jumping from her Massachusetts home’s second-floor window in January 2023. Within minutes, they were racing into the basement after her then husband screamed that all three of their children were dead.
“I can’t wake them up – I can’t get them up!” Patrick Clancy frantically told the officers who, along with firefighters and paramedics, gave jurors first-hand accounts on Thursday of the aftermath.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lindsay Clancy’s husband told police children were dead, court hears

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mayor announces resignation of Shon Barnes after city officials faced criticism over response to Sunday shooting
Seattle’s police chief has resigned amid criticism of the city’s response to a fatal shootout at a food festival last weekend, Katie Wilson, the mayor, said on Thursday.
The announcement followed hours of speculation about whether Shon Barnes would step down, as some of his supporters said he had rebuffed Wilson’s request that he resign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seattle police chief resigns after deadly food festival shooting

articles.author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
articles.description:
Both MPs have had the parliamentary whip restored following separate independent disciplinary processes 
MPs Diane Abbott and Joani Reid have been readmitted into Labour and had the parliamentary whip restored, just under two weeks into Andy Burnham’s premiership.
The party confirmed that this followed separate independent disciplinary processes, although Labour said the leadership played no role in either decision.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Diane Abbott and Joani Reid readmitted as Labour MPs

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
State department ‘takes full responsibility’ for erroneous, widely shared chart displayed at Aids conference in Brazil
A US government map of Africa mislabeled every country during a state department presentation at a ⁠global conference in Brazil ⁠this week, ​causing a stir among attenders who took screenshots and posted them online.
Reuters viewed a video of the presentation given at the Aids 2026 conference in ⁠Rio de Janeiro, which shows the errant map displayed halfway during a presentation about the state department’s new health agreements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US government map of Africa mislabels every country at global conference

articles.author: Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
Former lieutenant governor says path to Democratic nomination no longer viable as democratic socialist rival surges ahead
Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of the Democratic primary for governor on Thursday, upending the high-stakes contest less than two weeks before the 11 August election.
Barnes announced the decision in a video posted on social media, saying he no longer saw a viable path to the nomination, as democratic socialist Francesca Hong surged ahead with a commanding lead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mandela Barnes drops out of high-stakes Wisconsin governor’s race

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Local leaders say plan will transform funding so English regions no longer rely on Whitehall handouts for projects
England’s regional mayors will be able to break out of the “death grip of the Treasury” by borrowing to invest in big projects under “transformational” plans to shift power out of Whitehall.
For the first time, mayors will keep a share of income tax generated in their area from 2028, as well as business rates totalling tens of millions of pounds by April 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to free mayors from ‘Treasury death grip’ with new devolved powers

articles.author: Pippa Neill and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Major incident declared, with Sizewell B power station monitoring blaze and RSPB nature reserve badly hit
Hundreds of people have been evacuated and a major incident declared after a wildfire spread over more than 80 hectares (200 acres) on the coast of Suffolk, just a few miles from the Sizewell B nuclear power station.
The fire – which had been described by one witness as “apocalyptic” – was said to be stabilising on Thursday night. The statement was posted by Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service, which said at least 12 fire crews were remaining overnight in the area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds evacuated after ‘apocalyptic’ wildfire near Suffolk nuclear power station

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
CRS officers funded by UK tried to stop boarding of boat, on day four asylum seekers died trying to cross Channel
French riot police funded by UK taxpayers used teargas on asylum seekers in an attempt to stop them from boarding a boat in which three women were later found dead, a charity has claimed.
Footage and photographs seen by the Guardian show CS gas canisters being fired towards groups of people on Plage du Braek near Dunkirk at 4am on Thursday. At 6am, three women were found dead in a boat near the same beach.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: French riot police used teargas on people trying to board small boat, charity claims

articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
Figures show hot, dry, windy conditions in EU are 43% more severe than the average over last 20 years
Fire weather in the EU has broken records for severity for this time of year, data shows, as firefighters race to extinguish blazes across the Mediterranean.
Inflamed by carbon pollution, the hot, dry and windy weather across the EU from the start of the year until the end of July has been 43% more severe than the average for the same period over the last two decades, data from the European Forest Fire Information Service (Effis) shows.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Race to extinguish blazes across Europe as fire weather breaks records

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Yemeni sources say Saudis concentrating forces for what could be attack in central Yemen
Saudi Arabia is preparing for a major military offensive against the Houthis by sea and possibly by land in central Yemen, Yemeni sources believe, in a move to break the chokehold on its oil exports through the southern Red Sea.
Saudi forces have been seen withdrawing from the east of Yemen in what could be preparation for a land offensive. At the same time, Riyadh is trying to organise a naval coalition to protect shipping from Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab strait.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia prepares sea and possible land offensive against Houthis

articles.author: Aram Roston in Washington
articles.description:
Strike on Terminal Autonomy plant appears to be first time in the war that Moscow has targeted a US company
A drone factory in Kyiv destroyed by a Russian ballistic missile on Friday was owned by a US corporation registered in Delaware, in what appears to be the first time Moscow has targeted a US company in the conflict.
Terminal Autonomy makes precision “deep-strike” drones with guidance systems that are resistant to Russian jamming signals, according to a person familiar with the company.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russian missile destroys US firm’s Kyiv drone factory

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
UK’s highest court gives permission for Huda Ammori to challenge court of appeal ruling 
The co-founder of Palestine Action has won permission to challenge the ban against the group at the UK’s highest court.
The direct action group was proscribed as a terrorist organisation in July last year but its co-founder, Huda Ammori, has been fighting to have the ban overturned amid a mass civil disobedience campaign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Supreme court says Palestine Action co-founder can challenge ban on group

articles.author: Peter Beaumont and agencies
articles.description:
Polish PM visits scene of crater thought to have occurred during deadly wave of attacks on Ukraine
Russia has been accused of violating Polish airspace, after a missile exploded in a field in the east of the country, triggering Nato air defences, in the midst of a massive air raid that killed 13 people in neighbouring Ukraine.
Polish authorities said that the explosion near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia, close to Lublin, had created a 10-metre-wide crater. Residents of Tarnawa-Kolonia reported hearing an explosion at about 4am that shook the windows of their homes, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia accused of violating Polish airspace after missile explosion near village

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Electoral Commission urged to look into donations made by mother of convicted fraudster

Revealed: George Cottrell transferred $2m to his mother days before her donations to Reform UK

Labour has accused Reform UK of being “up to its neck in sleaze” as it called on the Electoral Commission to urgently investigate substantial donations made to the party by the mother of a convicted fraudster.
Bridget Phillipson, Labour’s new chair, called on the commission to examine whether any rules had been broken, after revelations in the Guardian that George Cottrell transferred more than $2m to his mother in the days before her donations to the party in 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour says Reform ‘up to its neck in sleaze’ and demands investigation into donations

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Maria and Czeslaw Krupa, who arrived as children of displaced Polish veterans, told they have no post-Brexit rights to return home to Bury
Two Polish citizens who have lived in the UK for nearly 80 years after their parents fled the second world war have spoken of their terrifying experience after being told they did not have post-Brexit rights to return to the UK.
In May, while visiting Poland, they learned that although they had been welcomed as refugees after the war, they now needed special post-Brexit paperwork to return to their home in Bury, Greater Manchester.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It was a big shock’: new border rules left couple stuck in Kraków after living in UK for 80 years

articles.author: William Christou in Beirut
articles.description:
Central Command says strikes aimed at diminishing Iranian military while mediators say talks are continuing

Middle East crisis – live updates

The US struck Iran overnight and Tehran retaliated at US allies in the region, reigniting the low-intensity, tit-for-tat war as mediators struggled to pull the two countries back to the negotiating table.
The US carried out overnight strikes on Iran – the first in more than five days – hours after Donald Trump vowed to hit the country “very hard” following Tehran’s targeting of a base in Jordan that hosts American troops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US hits dozens of targets in Iran overnight as peace efforts under threat

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Government fears social discontent on ‘most important battlefield’ of economy and livelihoods as war takes its toll amid anti-state dissent

Middle East crisis live – latest updates

Iran, in the middle of an escalating five-month war with the US, continues to stumble from one internal crisis to another – whether it is over public executions, the rising cost of living, the alleged bias of the state broadcaster or even the post-midnight destruction of pavements outside liberal-leaning Tehran cafes. Very little that happens in Iran, cultural or political, momentous or trivial, does so uncontested.
But there is now a growing threat of a long diplomatic deadlock, forged by mutual distrust in which neither side believes the other will stick to any agreement. That impasse has occurred as the war broadens, drawing in Yemen, Iraq and now Egypt. In Iran, at least, the advocates of escalation are winning. As a result, a convergence of Iran’s conflicts, internal and external, becomes more likely.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran’s war with the US is not its only conflict as internal crises mount

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Sam Mostyn says there is a widespread ‘failure to understand and engage with’ civic underpinnings of our democracy

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia faces a “growing catastrophe” from poor understanding of the country’s constitutional foundation, the governor general, Sam Mostyn, has warned as attacks on institutions and threats against elected officials undermine democratic participation.
Two years after her appointment as King Charles’s representative in Canberra, and as she brings a modern touch to the role of vice regal, Mostyn said that knowledge of how the country’s system of government operates was in steady decline and better civics education was needed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Governor general warns of ‘growing catastrophe’ that threatens to undermine democracy in Australia

articles.author: Dan Jervis-Bardy
articles.description:
The opposition leader is the highest-profile person mentioned so far at the NSW anti-corruption commission – and the political figure with the most to lose

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

After the opening days of an inquiry exposing a dark underbelly of the New South Wales Liberals, the prevailing mood among Angus Taylor’s colleagues is one of apprehension.
The federal opposition leader is not a specific target of Operation Rosny, which is investigating allegations of corruption against people associated with the NSW branch. He is not accused of wrongdoing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Icac revelations have left Angus Taylor’s colleagues anxious – and his factional enemies angry

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi
articles.description:
Analysis of samples collected from carcasses found traces of toxic chemical compound, says Kenya Wildlife Service
The recent deaths of 15 elephants near a park in southern Kenya in the past month were likely caused by the animals ingesting pesticides used on nearby tomato farms, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) has said.
Erustus Kanga, the agency’s director general, told Citizen TV that analysis of samples collected from the carcasses had found traces of cyanide, a chemical compound used in farming as a predator control poison and a pest fumigant, which has also been used by poachers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fifteen elephant deaths at Kenya park may be due to cyanide poisoning

articles.author: Giovanni Wanneh in Buea and Eromo Egbejule in Accra
articles.description:
Cameroon’s Paul Biya has not made a statement or been seen since leaving for ‘brief private stay’ at Swiss hotel on 7 June
A record 53-day absence by the world’s oldest head of state has renewed speculation in his native Cameroon about whether he is dead or alive, even though discussing his health is illegal in the country.
On 7 June, 93-year-old Paul Biya left for Switzerland for what officials described as a “brief private stay” alongside his wife, Chantal. Almost two months later, neither the president nor the first lady have addressed the country or been seen publicly.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fifty-three days and counting: 93-year-old leader’s record absence fuels health speculation

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo
articles.description:
Soldiers and emergency teams search damaged shopping centre, paper mill and homes for survivors

Earthquake rocks southern Japanese island of Kyushu – in pictures

The death toll from the powerful earthquake that hit Japan on Tuesday has risen to 30, as the search for survivors trapped in a badly damaged shopping centre, paper mill and collapsed homes across the south-west of the country continues.
The 6.8-magnitude quake, which struck Kumamoto prefecture on the island of Kyushu, injured at least 62 people, according to the prefectural government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Death toll in Japan earthquake rises to 30 as aftershock and heat hamper rescue efforts

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
Losing funds should force leaders to confront their own challenges, they said, while many voiced concerns over increasing foreign influence 
A quarter of young Africans believe aid cuts by the US could have a positive impact, saying that losing foreign money will force leaders to confront and solve their own challenges, according to a new survey.
In Ghana and Nigeria, almost half (41% and 40% respectively) of young people aged 18 to 24 were optimistic, with Liberia not far behind (37%). A further one in 10 (11%) young people were uncertain about the impact, according to the African Youth Survey, which interviewed almost 5,000 people across 16 of the continent’s 54 recognised countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A quarter of young Africans believe USAID cuts could be positive, survey finds

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Taz Ali (earlier)
articles.description:
Emergency workers are continuing their search for survivors in southern Japan after yesterday’s powerful earthquake 

‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing

An aerial view of a collapsed section of a bridge in the city of Yatsushiro after an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan’s southern Kumamoto prefecture:
Japan’s Mainichi Shimbun newspaper has been speaking to people at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro, where a chimney collapsed on to the site. 

 “I never imagined something like this would happen,” said a 33-year-old man who worked at the factory. “I never thought that the chimney could collapse. I’m worried about the people inside.”

 He was off duty and at home when the earthquake struck, and was unharmed. The names of those rescued and those trapped have not yet been released. “Someone I know might be affected,” he said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescue teams face ‘race against time’ in search for trapped survivors as death toll in Japan rises to at least 13 – as it happened

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo
articles.description:
Rescuers pulling people from the wreckage in southern Japan in a haunting repeat of disaster that struck 10 years ago

‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing

“There was a voice coming from the collapsed house, and I could see a hand,” Tomohide Nagata, a volunteer firefighter, told the Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbun. “One of our senior members crawled in and pulled him out. He was bleeding from the head, but I’m so glad he survived.”
Nagata had heard a noise coming from one completely flattened home in the rural town of Hikawa, close to the epicentre of Tuesday’s 6.8-magnitude earthquake in southern Japan. The town was one of the areas hardest hit, with numerous older houses collapsing. Terrified of the ongoing aftershocks, many residents spent Tuesday night in their cars outside Hikawa’s town hall, where staff distributed food and drinks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The shaking was terrifying’: stories of survival and loss emerge after Japan earthquake

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo, and Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Military mobilises thousands of personnel after quake on southern Kyushu island that registered a maximum 7 on the Japanese shindo intensity scale

Earthquake rocks southern Japanese island of Kyushu – in pictures 

At least 13 people were killed when a 6.8 magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan on Tuesday, injuring hundreds and knocking out power and water to tens of thousands.
“There are people who are still waiting to be rescued, and it’s a race against time,” the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, said on Wednesday. “We will go all out to find and rescue as many people as we can.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Potential toxic substance detected in several of 15 elephants found dead in Kenya’s Amboseli national park

Officials are investigating the deaths of 15 elephants over the past month in Kenya’s Amboseli national park.
The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said 10 of the elephants showed signs of partial paralysis before dying within two days.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenya investigating unexpected deaths of 15 elephants in national park

articles.author: Dara Kerr and agencies
articles.description:
Move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US
The Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national security. The move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US.
The FCC defines the banned robots as “advanced robotic devices”, which include humanoids and animal-like quadrupeds.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’

articles.author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
articles.description:
Data shows Canadians have replaced US vacations with other international trips in apparent rebuke to Trump
Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to the US in 2025 than in the previous year, as Donald Trump’s hostile policies towards his northern neighbour continue to incur an economic cost, new government data shows.
The research also indicates that Canadians are not bucking travel overall and instead have replaced US vacations with other international destinations, in a rebuke to Trump’s tariff regime and the president’s continued musings on annexing Canada.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to US in 2025 after Trump’s return to office

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Local civil rights group alleges authorities removed evidence of killings amid communications blackout
At least 30 people are alleged to have been killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in the past two days as part of what has been claimed is a brutal state crackdown that has engulfed the disputed region for weeks.
According to a local civil society group, Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), the Pakistani security services fired on tens of thousands of peaceful protesters, killing 25 people on Monday and five more on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan accused of fatally shooting 30 unarmed protesters in Kashmir

articles.author: Oliver Milman
articles.description:
Three years after Maui wildfires many still struggle with ‘biological, emotional and social consequences’, study says
A spate of ferocious wildfires across North America and Europe, worsened by the climate crisis, has incinerated homes and forests and forced thousands of people to flee. Previous fires suggest the effects of these blazes may linger for years to come.
The current fires and their plumes of smoke can appear to be a temporary, if immediate, crisis. Nearly 1,000 fires have sprung into life in the boreal forests of Canada, causing the evacuation of towns and toxic smoke to waft into major Canadian and US cities, prompting threats of retribution from Donald Trump, who bizarrely accused Canada of “poisoning” his country’s air.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Past fires suggest effects of Europe and North America wildfires may linger for years

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
President also blames Brazil and Mexico and says online critics ‘do not want the ideas of freedom to succeed’
More than a week has passed since Ferran Torres scored the extra-time goal that gave Spain its second World Cup, but – at least for Argentina’s president – the tournament is not over.
Javier Milei has claimed that a coordinated “anti-Argentina campaign” was behind criticism of the country’s team, accusations of racism among its fans and conspiracy theories alleging that Lionel Messi’s side was secretly being favoured by Fifa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Javier Milei accuses US Democrats of financing ‘anti-Argentina campaign’ at World Cup

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Cockroach Janta party says government has broken promise, with detentions in Delhi, Assam, West Bengal and Bihar
India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement, whose nationwide protests forced the resignation of the education minister, has accused the government of backtracking on its promise not to act against student protesters and has threatened to restart demonstrations.
The Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which organised mass protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said it had received reports of hundreds of students being detained or “harassed” by police.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement threatens to restart protests after mass student arrests

articles.author: John Bartlett in Santiago
articles.description:
Nelson Haase Mazzei was sentenced for murdering Jara in 2023, but fled from authorities in Chile
More than 50 years after the murder of the Chilean folk singer Víctor Jara, the last man wanted in connection with his death has been tracked down and brought to justice.
Nelson Haase Mazzei, a retired colonel, fled from authorities in 2023 after he and six other retired soldiers were sentenced in absentia for murdering Jara and another man.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pinochet-era soldier jailed for killing folk singer Víctor Jara 53 years ago

articles.author: Agence France-Press in Montreal
articles.description:
No one was injured and no suspects have been identified in connection to shooting near Toronto compound, police say
Shots were fired near the US consulate in Toronto early on Monday but no one was injured in the second shooting near the diplomatic compound in four months.
“Officers heard a firearm being discharged in the area,” and “a white sedan was seen fleeing the scene”, Toronto police said on X.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shots fired near US consulate in Canada for second time in four months

articles.author: Brendan Wood for MetDesk
articles.description:
Wind and record-breaking heat are fuelling the continent’s explosive fire season, with Spain and France among worst hit

Explainer: what is a ‘fire cloud’, and how have they worsened wildfires in Europe?

Europe wildfires live – latest updates

A combination of an unusually wet winter, very low rainfall since spring and repeated record-breaking summer heatwaves is likely to explain why wildfires have ignited, spread and resisted control so readily across France and Spain in recent days.
About 90% of wildfires are started by human activity, typically igniting “fine fuels” such as vegetation grass, pine needles, litter and twigs. And recent weather has almost certainly made ignition far easier. Drought in western Europe has turned this vegetation – which normally dries after only a few hours of heat and low rainfall – into tinder.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weather tracker: Why Europe’s wildfires are proving so fierce and difficult to stop

articles.author: Hettie O'Brien
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: Across ​the country, a ​younger generation is turning private disillusionment into public defiance​ against a government that once felt untouchable
Good morning. As flames engulfed parts of France and Spain this weekend, in India, the prime minister, Narendra Modi, was trying to put out a very different kind of fire. Thousands of people arrived in Delhi on Saturday to demand the resignation of his education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan. When he stepped down in the early afternoon, the protests turned into a triumphant block party.
But the Cockroach protests that have swept through India this summer are about much more than a single minister. They have humiliated Modi and undermined the indomitable power of his Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) that has ruled India for the…
articles.title: Monday briefing: ​How the Cockroach ​protests ​have expose​d the ​cracks in ​India’s government

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Ally forced to resign, with opposition parties reinvigorated and strongman leader’s grip over media channels rocked
Even the night before Narendra Modi accepted the resignation of his education minister, India’s prime minister appeared confident that the largest mass uprising to take place in his 12 years in power would do little to rattle his government.
Addressing his “young friends” in a late-night Instagram selfie reel on Friday, he thanked the people – who were mobilised en masse across the country, shouting anti-government slogans – for their “thoughtful suggestions”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party protest victory signals trouble ahead for Modi

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Anna Betts, Shannon Ho, Lucy Campbell, Rachel Leingang and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
Republicans senators Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted in favor of the motion to prevent Trump from continuing hostilities against Iran. This blog is now closed.

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

The US economy expanded at a sluggish 1.5% pace from April through June as rising imports weighed on growth. But consumer spending rose. And the Federal Reserve’s favored measure of inflation grew more slowly last month despite remaining above the central bank’s 2% target.
The commerce department reported today that growth in US gross domestic product (GDP) – the nation’s output of goods and services – decelerated from 2.1% in the first three months of 2026 and came in below economists’ expectations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senate’s latest effort to halt Trump’s Iran hostilities fails in 49-50 vote as some Republicans side with Democrats – as it happened

articles.author: Roque Planas
articles.description:
US government, which owes legal services firm $65m, stopped paying in December, as contract runs out Friday 
Current and former prosecutors are denouncing the Trump administration for fast-tracking the deportation of immigrant children, as a key contract for legal services is set to expire on Friday.
A series of federal laws has for decades shielded child immigrants from removal, either to protect their safety or to allow them to testify against abusers or human traffickers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump administration to let contract aiding unaccompanied minors expire

articles.author: Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
Former lieutenant governor says path to Democratic nomination no longer viable as democratic socialist rival surges ahead
Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of the Democratic primary for governor on Thursday, upending the high-stakes contest less than two weeks before the 11 August election.
Barnes announced the decision in a video posted on social media, saying he no longer saw a viable path to the nomination, as democratic socialist Francesca Hong surged ahead with a commanding lead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mandela Barnes drops out of high-stakes Wisconsin governor’s race

articles.author: Anna Betts
articles.description:
Kathryn Ruemmler was blasted by family of late Virginia Giuffre after House committee transcripts were released

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email 

A former White House counsel and former general counsel of Goldman Sachs, who has faced scrutiny over her past ties to Jeffrey Epstein, told a House committee this month that some of the allegations made by one of his most prominent accusers “lacked inherent credibility”, according to newly released transcripts.
Kathryn Ruemmler’s name appeared thousands of times in records related to Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender, that were released earlier this year by the US Department of Justice under the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-White House counsel says Epstein accuser’s testimony ‘lacked inherent credibility’

articles.author: Sam Levine
articles.description:
Republican senators sought written limits on settlement, but president held firm despite risk to attorney general pick

US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump’s refusal to officially end a hugely controversial agreement giving him broad tax immunity and creating a $1.8bn slush fund underscored how the US president’s own self-interest takes precedence above all else in his government.
For weeks, Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, has said that the slush fund portion of the agreement was dead. And for a few brief hours on Wednesday, it seemed that the president might agree to a relatively modest request from two Republican senators to put in writing that there were certain limits on an extraordinary tax immunity deal. After all, it seemed like a small price to pay in exchange for getting Blanche, a staunch Trump loyalist who previously served as his personal lawyer, confirmed permanently as the US attorney general.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s tax immunity scheme hoists president by his own petard on Blanche AG nomination

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
The conservative columnist Ross Douthat is the network’s latest perplexing hire – but the move is in line with the new leadership
In media circles, this week’s hire of a prominent New York Times columnist as a correspondent for CBS’s 60 Minutes was greeted with disbelief.
The collective response went something like this: “What?!”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No TV experience? At CBS News, that’s no problem | Margaret Sullivan

articles.author: Sunny Patel
articles.description:
Francesca Hong, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, is part of a wave of democratic socialists finding traction with an old idea
In a matter of weeks, Francesca Hong, an unlikely candidate for governor in one of the country’s most heated battleground states, will test a message that is at once radical and, to many, incredibly practical: the government should help pay for childcare.
“When we talk about free childcare, you can connect to folks whether it’s on an economic argument or just purely that it’s the right thing to do for our kids,” said Hong, a democratic socialist running in Wisconsin’s Democratic primary on 11 August. “I always like to remind folks: if we don’t take care of our kids, who’s going to take care of us?”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How free childcare started winning US elections: ‘Overnight, people realized how essential it was’

articles.author: Matt Gurney
articles.description:
The White House fails to understand that Mark Carney and Canada’s regional leaders can’t cave in to the US president: it’s too toxic to voters
• Matt Gurney is a journalist based in Toronto
Though many hate to admit it, Canadians have long wished for more attention from the US. Well, we’re getting it now. And it turns out that President Trump and some of his top supporters in the Maga movement don’t much like us.
The first big hint was when he started talking about annexing us, saying we couldn’t survive without American support. But the most recent example of Trump’s dislike for Canada can be seen in his latest tariff policies. Canada was largely spared the impact of his “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025 by its pre-existing free trade deal with the US (and Mexico), but earlier this month, as expected, the US declined to extend that deal for another 16-year term. It’s now subject to annual renegotiations. Then, last week, the White House announced tariffs as high as 50% on a selection of Canadian products including, for the first time, items previously protected by the trade agreement. The US called it retaliation for Canadian trade practices.
Matt Gurney is a journalist based in Toronto, and co-editor of The Line, an online magazine
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump has singled out us Canadians for special treatment in his tariff war – there is no choice but to get nasty | Matt Gurney

articles.author: Aaron Gell
articles.description:
J Street’s liberal Zionist politics are landing with the Democratic establishment but the electorate may have moved on
When Daniel Biss addressed his supporters after clinching the Democratic nomination in Illinois’s ninth congressional district this past March, he did something politicians rarely do: he paid homage to a lobby group.
“This victory belongs to J Street,” Biss declared.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aipac’s brand has become toxic. Can this ‘pro-Israel, pro-peace’ rival move in?

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
The US vice-president is facing a barrage of allegations and complaints from inside and outside the Republican ranks. Good news for Marco Rubio – but not for the rest of the world
There’s something a bit off about JD Vance. And I mean that literally: the vice-president has been snacking on sauerkraut and other fermented foods as part of a weight-loss regime. Health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr got a number of Trump officials, including Vance, on to the diet, and is thrilled with the results. “Within 20 days I lost 20 pounds,” Kennedy said at an event in Michigan last month. “JD Vance is also on the diet and you can see how different he looks.” Dunno about that: still looks like a naked opportunist to me.
If you want to get into Donald Trump’s good books, improving your looks is a surefire way to do so. According to MS Now, the president is loving Vance’s svelte new figure; it’s helped propel him back into Trump’s good graces. Which is lucky for him because he doesn’t have many other fans. They may be full of beneficial bacteria, but everyone around Vance seems to hate his guts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Even Maga is falling out of love with JD Vance. If only his rivals weren’t even worse … | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Is it normal for a sitting senator to have to routinely submit proofs of life to a public who suspect he might be braindead? Just asking for 340 million friends 
Is it normal for a sitting senator to have to routinely submit proofs of life to a public who suspect he might be braindead? Just asking for 340 million friends in the US. Mitch McConnell was hospitalized for a medical event on 14 June and we are now in week six of What on Earth Is Going on With Mitch? – a mystery that has riveted the nation.
According to McConnell’s team there isn’t actually a mystery at all. The 84-year-old is doing great, they want us to know. So great that they have now released two photos to prove it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Welcome to America, where you’re never quite sure if your senator is dead or not | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Owen Myers
articles.description:
The comedian and actor’s new Netflix special is a gleefully absurd take on politics and potty-mouthed humor
Mary Beth Barone knows exactly who will be offended by her new Netflix special. “JK Rowling, Republicans, establishment Democrats, the British, the Irish and Zionists,” she tells me, reading a list from her Notes app. Then there’s “Katy Kats – which is what Katy Perry calls her fans – and male comedians and one specific girl named Tatiana”. When informed that this encompasses over half of the population of the US, she beams.
Barone’s comedy is a delicate balance between sweetness and cynicism. In her standup she’ll adopt a ditzy pose while she tears down morally bankrupt politicians, sends up cis male entitlement or implores her audience to have sex with moderates in the hope of bringing them over to the left. In the past five years, she has edged her way closer to the mainstream with a Comedy Central web-series, a couple of standup spots on Jimmy Fallon’s late-night show, and a podcast co-hosted with her friend Benito Skinner that is so popular it has its own merch line. The past 12 months have seen her career go into overdrive: now she is the co-lead of a wildly popular TV show (Overcompensating, created by Skinner), chats to the A-list on the Golden Globes’ red carpet and sits front row at New York fashion week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mary Beth Barone on provocative jokes, Palestine and manosphere misogyny: ‘It’s hard to stomach that those are my co-workers’

articles.author: George Chidi in Marietta, Georgia, Shrai Popat in North York, Maine, Rachel Leingang in Superior, Wisconsin, and Joseph Gedeon in Washington. Graphics by Andrew Witherspoon
articles.description:
Whether in favor of or against the US-Israel war on Iran, people across the country are left holding the bill and wondering on its purpose
Five months after the United States and Israel started a historically unpopular war against Iran that was going to supposedly last weeks, the fighting has refused to resolve in victory, defeat or peace. Iran’s supreme leader had been killed in the opening strikes, ceasefires broke down, and the strait of Hormuz has been closed and reopened.
For voters interviewed across the country, while the damage may be distant, the residual effects have shown up at the pump, on the grocery bill and in a phone call telling a spouse they have a day to report for deployment. And for a country still absorbing the aftermath of Israel’s war on Gaza – funded to the tune of billions of dollars by the United States – the war in Iran lands on top of an already raw argument about what American power is for.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Americans feel pinch of continued Iran war: ‘It’s screwed everything up’

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with David Smith and Rachel Leingang . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this year, Congress reached a depressing milestone: 86% of Americans, a record high, disapproved of its job performance. But this summer, there have been some signs that shifts are underway. On the left, House Democrats have just voted in unprecedented numbers to withhold military aid from Israel, and across the country, progressive candidates are running competitive primary campaigns that are energizing a base fed up with the status quo. On the right, Republicans are reeling from the sudden death of Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator and one of Donald Trump's staunchest supporters. Mitch McConnell, the former Senate majority leader, remains sequestered following a health scare in June, raising questions of if a changing of the guard might be underway there, too. Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief and Rachel Leingang, midwest political correspondent, to discuss gerontocracy, transparency, the rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and just how much of an inflection point this summer might be for both parties


This page was amended on 23 July 2026. A previous version misspelled Lindsey Graham. 

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is US Congress finally on the verge of a change? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Hosted by Jonathan Freedland . Produced by May Robson, Jacob Liebenberg, Ned Carter Miles and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj .
articles.description:
The debate about how old is too old to serve in public office has resurfaced this week after the shock death of the Republican senator Lindsey Graham and the surprise return of Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old senator who published a photo of himself in hospital after a long absence from the spotlight.
With rumours continuing to swirl around Donald Trump’s health, why is it US politicians seem to cling on to power for so long?
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Alexis Coe, a presidential historian and columnist for the New York Times Book review, about whether the US is becoming a gerontocracy – and what can be done about it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are American politicians too old? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with Shrai Popat and Lauren Gambino . Produced by Meg Driscoll, edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this week, Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, was accused by a former partner of sexual assault. Platner denies the allegations, but on Wednesday, he suspended his campaign, accusing the “political establishment” of tanking his candidacy. But this is only the most recent scandal to have surfaced around Platner’s campaign — over the past year, the oyster farmer and combat veteran was revealed to have a tattoo that closely resembled a Totenkopf (a widely recognized Nazi symbol), a long paper trail of racist, misogynist and homophobic posts on Reddit, and in June, the New York Times published allegations from three former partners about Platner’s “toxic” behavior in their relationships, including, in several cases, physical intimidation (allegations Platner denied).
As Democrats regroup and evaluate their dwindling chances to flip the Senate in November, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian political reporters Lauren Gambino and Shrai Popat to ask why voters flocked to Platner, why they were reluctant to abandon him as the scandals came out — and what the whole mess says about who gets the privilege of political redemption.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Graham Platner wasn’t the answer to the Democrats’ man problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
articles.description:
Both MPs have had the parliamentary whip restored following separate independent disciplinary processes 
MPs Diane Abbott and Joani Reid have been readmitted into Labour and had the parliamentary whip restored, just under two weeks into Andy Burnham’s premiership.
The party confirmed that this followed separate independent disciplinary processes, although Labour said the leadership played no role in either decision.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Diane Abbott and Joani Reid readmitted as Labour MPs

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Water levels across several of Europe’s major waterways have dropped to exceptionally low levels, setting new records in some areas.
Extreme heat exacerbated by the climate crisis is intensifying the drought hitting the continent as record-breaking heatwaves means the hot atmosphere is evaporating water from rivers, lakes, soils and plants quickly.
The Danube has hit the lowest level of water in 30 years in several countries including Hungary, Serbia and Romania, and the Rhine has dropped to its lowest recorded level in some sections and is expected to drop further due to drought


Climate crisis-driven heat ‘sucking soils dry’ as extreme drought hits Europe

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Record low water levels across Europe reveal mammoth skeletons and forgotten shipwrecks – video

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Local leaders say plan will transform funding so English regions no longer rely on Whitehall handouts for projects
England’s regional mayors will be able to break out of the “death grip of the Treasury” by borrowing to invest in big projects under “transformational” plans to shift power out of Whitehall.
For the first time, mayors will keep a share of income tax generated in their area from 2028, as well as business rates totalling tens of millions of pounds by April 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to free mayors from ‘Treasury death grip’ with new devolved powers

articles.author: Pippa Neill and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Major incident declared, with Sizewell B power station monitoring blaze and RSPB nature reserve badly hit
Hundreds of people have been evacuated and a major incident declared after a wildfire spread over more than 80 hectares (200 acres) on the coast of Suffolk, just a few miles from the Sizewell B nuclear power station.
The fire – which had been described by one witness as “apocalyptic” – was said to be stabilising on Thursday night. The statement was posted by Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service, which said at least 12 fire crews were remaining overnight in the area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds evacuated after ‘apocalyptic’ wildfire near Suffolk nuclear power station

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
CRS officers funded by UK tried to stop boarding of boat, on day four asylum seekers died trying to cross Channel
French riot police funded by UK taxpayers used teargas on asylum seekers in an attempt to stop them from boarding a boat in which three women were later found dead, a charity has claimed.
Footage and photographs seen by the Guardian show CS gas canisters being fired towards groups of people on Plage du Braek near Dunkirk at 4am on Thursday. At 6am, three women were found dead in a boat near the same beach.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: French riot police used teargas on people trying to board small boat, charity claims

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
UK’s highest court gives permission for Huda Ammori to challenge court of appeal ruling 
The co-founder of Palestine Action has won permission to challenge the ban against the group at the UK’s highest court.
The direct action group was proscribed as a terrorist organisation in July last year but its co-founder, Huda Ammori, has been fighting to have the ban overturned amid a mass civil disobedience campaign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Supreme court says Palestine Action co-founder can challenge ban on group

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
PM tells reporters the government cannot ignore the energy resource ‘when people are struggling’
Andy Burnham has said he will take a “pragmatic” approach to oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, saying the government could not ignore the potential energy resources it holds.
The prime minister’s comments came in response to a question about his conversation with Donald Trump on his first day in No 10. Trump had said Burnham told him he would “open up” North Sea oil, something the UK summary of the call made no mention of.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham promises ‘pragmatic’ approach to North Sea oil and gas

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Electoral Commission urged to look into donations made by mother of convicted fraudster

Revealed: George Cottrell transferred $2m to his mother days before her donations to Reform UK

Labour has accused Reform UK of being “up to its neck in sleaze” as it called on the Electoral Commission to urgently investigate substantial donations made to the party by the mother of a convicted fraudster.
Bridget Phillipson, Labour’s new chair, called on the commission to examine whether any rules had been broken, after revelations in the Guardian that George Cottrell transferred more than $2m to his mother in the days before her donations to the party in 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour says Reform ‘up to its neck in sleaze’ and demands investigation into donations

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Maria and Czeslaw Krupa, who arrived as children of displaced Polish veterans, told they have no post-Brexit rights to return home to Bury
Two Polish citizens who have lived in the UK for nearly 80 years after their parents fled the second world war have spoken of their terrifying experience after being told they did not have post-Brexit rights to return to the UK.
In May, while visiting Poland, they learned that although they had been welcomed as refugees after the war, they now needed special post-Brexit paperwork to return to their home in Bury, Greater Manchester.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It was a big shock’: new border rules left couple stuck in Kraków after living in UK for 80 years

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Returns for breaches of licence conditions rose 31% in the first quarter of 2026, adding to pressure on prison places
More people were recalled to prison than were released during the first three months of 2026, the first time on record the “recall rate” has surpassed 100% in England and Wales.
Between January and March 2026, 12,977 people were released from prison while 13,193 people were returned to prison for breaching their licence conditions, up 31% from last year, new Ministry of Justice (MoJ) data showed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More prisoners in England and Wales are recalled than released for first time

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
‘There is a resource there. When people are struggling, we can’t ignore that,’ the prime minister says when asked about his conversation with Donald Trump
Q: [From ITV’s Romilly Weeks] You say that Reform UK followed all the rules in relation to donations. But why did George Cottrell give $2m to his mother shortly before she made substantial donations to the party?
Jenrick said Reform was certain all the rules were followed. Any questions for Cottrell would have to be directed to him, he said.
It does seem curious that in this case the police have chosen not to take action.
We’ll see whether they take action against the individual who posted the original tweet, who wore the T-shirt. I’m hearing today that the police may have closed that investigation as well. [See 9.20am.]
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham says he told Trump he would be ‘pragmatic’ on drilling for oil in North Sea – as it happened

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Shares in Rolls-Royce jump by 5% after it lifts earnings guidance, while BAE Systems also upgrades profit forecasts
Rolls-Royce and BAE Systems are expecting higher profits as governments around the world increase their defence spending.
Both companies lifted their earnings guidance on Thursday morning, citing commitments from governments to raise investment in defence systems.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Profits boost for UK defence firms as governments increase spending

articles.author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
articles.description:
Union calling for two paid breaks a day in what it says is punishing schedule for Storehouse ‘order an object’ workers
Staff at the V&A’s Storehouse site in east London have voted overwhelmingly to strike in a dispute over what they say are inadequate toilet and hydration breaks.
They will join staff across V&A sites in London who on Wednesday also voted to strike in a wider dispute over pay, working conditions, and the museum having declined to seek living wage accreditation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Staff at V&A site in London vote to strike over toilet and water breaks

Andy Burnham gave a major speech on Wednesday on his plans for a national care service. He sought cross-party consensus on the issue by speaking to the Tories and Lib Dems. articles.author: Rupert Jones
articles.description:
Laptops, phones and documents seized as information commissioner acts on messages about mis-selling scandal
Laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized after officials carried out search warrants in a crackdown on claims companies plaguing people with spam text messages about the car finance mis-selling scandal.
The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) executed warrants at homes and businesses linked to five companies in London, Liverpool, Bolton, Burnley and Swansea on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Raids across UK in crackdown on nuisance car finance texts

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Bank’s wariness about inflationary pressures from the conflict lie behind decision to hold steady at 3.75%

Business live – latest updates

There is a threat of high inflation coming to the UK but only from the conflict in the Middle East, which could keep oil prices high for much longer than was expected when Donald Trump first began attacking Iran.
It is the war that makes the difference between a benign outlook for inflation and one that puts it back on a rising trajectory, senior UK central bankers believe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Only the Middle East crisis is preventing a drop in UK interest rates

articles.author: Geneva Abdul and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Several councils to stop housing tenants in glass-fronted Britannia Point in London, where tenants were earlier told they could not use air con
As the fourth heatwave of the year hit the UK on Wednesday, Benice Bodah and her three teenage sons braced for more scorching temperatures inside their south-west London home. The two-bedroom flat has a built-in air-conditioning unit, but it has worked only intermittently in the almost three years since the family were placed in temporary accommodation at Britannia Point in Colliers Wood. “It has not been easy, but what can we do?” said Bodah, 48.
Several councils have now agreed to stop housing families in emergency accommodation in the glass-fronted block after the Guardian revealed they had been told they couldn’t use the air-conditioning during heatwaves as it had “not been offered as an amenity” for them. The 19-storey building is owned by Criterion Capital, set up by the billionaire property magnate Asif Aziz. The temporary tenancies can last from weeks to years and are managed separately by letting agencies, including the London-based Aura Assets Management.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Families to be moved out of billionaire-owned tower after suffering without air con

articles.author: Damian Carrington Environment editor
articles.description:
UKHSA estimates 2,877 fatalities during heatwaves in May and June, almost twice that recorded in 2025 season
England is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths this summer after the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves.
The record was set in 2022 with 2,985 deaths, and August, traditionally the hottest month, is yet to arrive. The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said: “My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: England on track for record heat-related deaths this summer, official data shows

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
Chief executive says the four-year plan will lead to greater efficiency but gives no details of potential job losses

Business live – latest updates



Lloyds Banking Group will cut another £2bn of costs as part of a four-year plan under which its chief executive will use new tech and AI to drive growth.
Charlie Nunn said the strategy, which the UK’s largest high street lender will launch in January, would involve investing £13bn into the business by 2030, including for “pioneering technology” to lure new business, improve efficiency and increase payouts for shareholders.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lloyds Bank to cut £2bn in costs as part of AI-powered strategy

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Bank’s chair pledges to keep up fight against inflation but decision brings fears of a failure to keep pace

Business live – latest updates

US government borrowing costs have hit their highest level since 2007 after the Federal Reserve voted to hold its key interest rate steady, feeding fears that the central bank may not move fast enough to tame a rise in inflation.
The yield – or interest rate – on the 30-year US Treasury bond rose 14 basis points to nearly 5.24%, a 19-year high, after the Fed announced its decision to hold its main rate at between 3.5% and 3.75% for the fifth meeting in a row.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US borrowing costs hit 19-year high as Fed holds interest rates

articles.author: Chris Baraniuk
articles.description:
Boom in migrating moth sightings put down to hot weather, strong winds and food scarcity in Europe

articles.description:
PC, Xbox, PlayStation 5; Halo Studios/Xbox Game Studios
Halo’s modernised introduction to all that was great about the 00s’ first-person shooter is also a welcome return trip for those of us who were there at the time
This 25th-anniversary remake of Xbox’s most iconic shooter comes loaded with symbolism. It arrives at a time when Xbox’s whole gaming division (and indeed the games business as a whole) is in turmoil. It’s been made by Halo Studios, an outfit that has arguably never quite recaptured the magic conjured by Halo: Combat Evolved’s original developer Bungie, a studio now owned by rival Sony. It has been polished and prettified using Unreal Engine 5, making it look and feel more modern at the expense of visual uniqueness: Halo now looks similar to hundreds of other games made with those same tools, where Bungie’s 2001 original, made with a bespoke engine, still looks austerely distinctive. I never wanted to become this person, but: perhaps things were  better in the old days?
I had my misgivings after the opening level, in which freshly defrosted supersoldier Master Chief fends off an alien attack on a disintegrating spaceship. Originally this was a masterclass in explosive action: you wake up, you look around (once a clever way to determine whether you needed to invert the controls), and you get right into it, firing gaming’s best pistol at chittering alien grunts who scatter from your bullets. Now it’s wrapped in needlessly expanded cutscenes and explanations. Where Halo Studios has made changes to Combat Evolved’s pacing, it really feels noticeable.

articles.author: Keith Stuart
articles.description:
James Cameron’s high-octane film sequel is a blueprint for modern action space slashers
• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
It is difficult to believe that James Cameron’s Aliens was released into cinemas 40 years ago. The seminal space shooter took the original Alien – a tense slasher film with a tiny cast and one monster – and transformed it into an intergalactic war movie crammed with wry one-liners, massive guns and an actual boss battle finale. As a 14-year-old, I stood in line at the Tatton Gatley cinema, unsure if I’d be allowed in – I came out three hours later a changed person, my head filled with esoteric military slang and a deep fear of beeping motion detectors. For days afterwards, I slept with my duvet covering my mouth so that no facehuggers could get me. (I was a highly impressionable teenager.)
It’s little wonder that the film has had such a profound effect on video game design. Take the colonial marines, for example. Although the concept of the space soldier had been around in sci-fi novels since the 1930s, most notably in the works of EE “Doc” Smith and Robert Heinlein (the Starship Troopers), Hicks, Hudson, Vasquez and co, were the perfect 80s rendition, combining the witty banter of contemporary buddy cop flicks with awesome weaponry and hi-tech gadgets. Their influence is easy to spot in Doom, where the nameless marine fights ceaseless waves of hellish monsters using a mix of futuristic rifles and good old shotguns. It’s there too in the Halo series, the Spartan soldiers sporting the same armour and mega weapons, cruising about in very similar highly militarised starships and fighting recognisable hive-mind space beasts. Gears of War, Killzone and Marathon all borrow from the same set of costumes and deadly accessories.

articles.description:
The new breed of camera-equipped streetlights has the potential to fight crime and track down missing persons. Or will it just take Britain one step closer to a surveillance state?
How would you feel if your neighbourhood lamp-posts could recognise your number plate, and also your face? Maybe you wouldn’t mind, given how long we’ve had automatic number plate recognition and CCTV. What about if that lamp-post could power itself through its own solar panels, and perhaps find another use for any extra power generated – that would be good, right? This is what Conflow Power Group (CPG) in Warwickshire claims for its iLamps, the first of their kind in the UK.
What if lamp-posts had the potential to incorporate new AI capability – gait analysis, suspicious behaviours – that you haven’t even heard of? This is what the organisation Big Brother Watch worries about. And what if the home secretary had explicitly said she believed in a “panopticon state” – that is, a state that could watch you at all times (as Shabana Mahmood already has) – and what if she still had a job when the lamp-post eyes got their updates? Or what if the next home secretary was even keener on hyper-surveillance (hard to imagine), and the street apparatus was already in place? What about all the data this would harvest – who would own it?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spies in the sky: how worried should we be about the arrival of AI-enabled smart lamp-posts?

Detective Grimoire is at it again in the long-awaited new entry to this stylish series of comedy whodunnits
In a boom time for mystery games, the Detective Grimoire series stands out for its style and sense of humour. The Mermaid Mask continues to build upon the formula laid down in Secret of the Swamp and polished in Tangle Tower, and while there is still room for further improvements this sequel is worth the seven years’ wait.
This time, the casually competent Grimoire and his smart if sarcastic sidekick Sally have been summoned to a submarine to solve the locked-room murder of its captain, Magnus Mortuga. You click around the cluttered rooms of the vessel to hear the detectives’ comedic commentary and look for clues and – closer up – click and drag to move objects around for further examination or to solve a puzzle. (For those playing on Nintendo Switch 2, the mouse controls are actually useful here, if not comfortable in the long run.)
